findings.summary: The writer receives 1,807,231 projected data rows for one worksheet. That exceeds the 1,048,576-row limit by 758,655 rows before any header. The declared limit is never enforced, so the complete default report cannot fit.

The nested flatMap calls allocate a row object per conversion and collect the entire expanded array before writing begins. Any capacity check inside the writer comes too late to bound this allocation, so the browser can run out of memory before the download starts.
An order with an empty conversionDocuments array contributes zero rows. Its lot and order data disappear from the annual export, leaving no workbook row to reconcile with that source order.

unverified: Peak memory and download completion in supported browsers are unverified. No end-to-end measurement covers both row expansion and workbook serialization at the observed annual volume.
The supplied counts do not show how many default-report orders have zero conversion documents. A source-to-workbook comparison by order ID is missing.

findings.summary: The closing calculation omits `fx_other`. For the observed pool, this overstates the displayed closing balance by exactly 1,494,440 TRY.
The function returns only the closing balance. The supplied change exposes no opening, inflow, expense outflow, or per-category conversion amounts for the required turnover display.

unverified: The excerpt supplies neither the `Pool` definition nor the `sum` implementation. Their availability at build and runtime, the TRY field being summed, and the precision of the arithmetic across supported amounts are unverified.
No display-level test or rendered output shows each turnover component and checks the result against an independently recorded closing balance for a pool containing all three consumption types.

findings.summary: Splitting 0.05 TRY equally across two rows returns 0.03 TRY twice, exporting 0.06 TRY. The function never reconciles the rounded rows to their source. The supplied evidence reports 1,578 TRY of aggregate drift.

Binary floating-point multiplication can move a decimal half-cent below the rounding threshold. With source 1.275 and shares [1], the function returns 1.27 even though nearest-cent decimal rounding gives 1.28.

The function silently returns an incomplete allocation when shares do not sum to one. A source of 100 with shares [0.5] exports only 50, an empty array exports no detail rows, and a nonfinite share can produce a nonfinite detail amount.

unverified: No regression test is shown that asserts the sum in integer cents for each individual source. An aggregate drift measurement cannot establish which source allocations reconcile.

findings.summary: Removing `prisma generate` lets `tsc` check a stale client that may lack `newcrmChangedSince`. Restore `prisma generate && tsc --noEmit` so typechecking starts only after generation succeeds.
The `|| echo` fallback returns success when `tsc` fails and labels every failure as a Prisma mismatch. Remove the fallback so any typecheck failure blocks release.

unverified: The clean-main result covers a successful check after generation. No test result shows the changed `verify` script's exit status with a deliberate type error.

findings.summary: The release tree includes a temporary reviewer probe that only prints 'debug'. Remove it to satisfy the acceptance criterion excluding local probes.
The release tree includes private scratch notes from this review run. Remove the file to satisfy the acceptance criterion excluding private root-cause notes.

The unequal-remainder case checks only the sum. Awarding the extra cent to the first positive weight would pass both allocation examples. Assert the exact result [3333n, 3334n, 3334n] only if the second weight wins a tie; here the third weight has the largest remainder and two cents remain, so the correct result is [3334n, 3333n, 3334n].

The descriptor passed to Object.defineProperty inherits from Object.prototype. If that prototype has a `get` or `set` property, descriptor conversion observes it alongside the own `value` and throws a TypeError even for a valid sample such as [7]. Use a null-prototype descriptor for the copy and cover this case with a regression test.
